newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks set new record fourth day in row.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks set new record fourth day in row.

text.p: Swiss shares ended at a new record high, the fourth consecutive record closing, just a shade off the 4,300 level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
The market was somewhat nervous about the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Meeting, so some profit taking could be seen off and on, dealers said.
However, dealers considered the possibility of an increase in U.S. interest rates as minimal.
Prospects remained favourable as buying interest was lively after several upgrades of the Swiss market by U.S. brokers, a trader noted.
The SMI ended up 13.7 points, or 0.32 percent, to 4,296.5, hitting an all-time high at 4,314.4 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 5.52 points, or 0.2 percent, to 2,742.78.
Trade was active in financials, dealers said. UBS, which led the active list, added nine francs to 1,202. SBC also firmed, while CS Group ended in a slight decline.
Novartis registered shares soared six francs to 1,656.
Roche certificates were boosted by favourable comments from analysts about new drugs and high demand for Roche options, dealers said. The certificates firmed 45 francs to 12,285.
Surveillance jumped 135 francs, or 4.29 percent, to 3,280, on buying by Geneva-based investors. One trader noted the share may have been propelled by a forthcoming study.
Swissair suffed from a downgrade by a bank and slumped 15 francs to 1,285.
